from_notes: Element: It is a form of matter that cannot be broken down by chemical reactions into simpler substances
x: Silver is an element, so it cannot be split further by chemical means. Sugar and water are compounds and air is a mixture.
source: OnlyIAS NCERT S&T Part 7 (src/science-tech/onlyias-ncert-science-tech-07.txt) p.1; PMF General Science Part 7 (src/science-tech/pmf-general-science-07.txt) p.7

from_notes: Germination of the seed happens when the seed is sown in the land and watered.
x: A seed needs water, air (oxygen) and a suitable temperature to germinate. Soil and sunlight are not essential; seeds sprout on wet cotton in the dark.
source: printed key, not verified in the library; standard textbook fact (NCERT Class 7/9 seed germination)

x: The fish internal ear (with its otoliths) works mainly as an organ of balance, the answer the keys give. Fish have no sound-producing ear, and water movement is sensed by the lateral line.
source: printed key, not verified in the library; standard textbook fact

from_notes: Heating | Infrared heaters, physiotherapy
x: Infrared rays warm the tissues and are used in physiotherapy for body aches. UV is used for sterilisation, and visible light has no such heating use.
Oryza sativa is cultivated rice. Wheat is Triticum, maize Zea mays and potato Solanum tuberosum.
source: printed key, not verified in the library; standard textbook fact

x: A butterfly has a long coiled proboscis for siphoning nectar. The mosquito pierces and sucks, the cockroach chews and the housefly sponges.
source: printed key, not verified in the library; standard textbook fact (NCERT Class 11 insect mouthparts)

from_notes: Bernoulli's Theorem is a fundamental principle in fluid dynamics
x: A is true: the wing's convex top makes air move faster above it. R is false because faster air on top means lower pressure on top than below, which gives lift.

from_notes: Red light has the longest wavelength and lowest energy, while violet light has the shortest wavelength and the highest energy.
x: A is false: red light is less energetic than green light. R is true: red light (~700 nm) has a longer wavelength than green (~530 nm), and energy falls as wavelength rises.

from_notes: Red light has the longest wavelength and lowest energy, while violet light has the shortest wavelength and the highest energy.
x: A is false because red light has less energy than green light. R is true because red light's wavelength (~700 nm) is longer than green's (~530 nm).

from_notes: For liquids, viscosity generally decreases with increasing temperature.
x: A is false because a liquid's viscosity, glycerin's included, falls as it warms. R is true: heating raises the molecules' kinetic energy, which is why the viscosity falls.

from_notes: It persists there for about 1/16th of a second.
x: Films are projected at 24 frames a second, so A is true. Books key R as false because NCERT puts persistence of vision at about 1/16 s, not 0.1 s.
dispute: Most books and keys: A true, R false (persistence = 1/16 s, NCERT). Strictly: persistence of vision is quoted as about 1/10 to 1/16 s and is the reason films run at 24 frames/s, so (a) is also argued.

x: White clothes reflect heat, so they suit summer, not winter. In winter, dark clothes that absorb heat are preferred, so A is false and R is true.
source: printed key, not verified in the library; standard textbook fact (NCERT Class 7 heat)

from_notes: Thus, the male determines the sex of the offspring.
x: A is false because the father's sperm (X or Y) decides the child's sex. R is true: women are XX and give only an X.

from_notes: Moon ≈ 1/6th of Earth weight
x: A is true because Moon's surface gravity is about 1/6 of Earth's. R is false: the Moon does have gravity, only weaker.
source: NextGen Rocket Physics (src/science-tech/rocket-physics.txt) p.97; OnlyIAS NCERT S&T Part 3 (src/science-tech/onlyias-ncert-science-tech-03.txt) p.1

x: A white top reflects the sun's heat. A black underside absorbs the heat radiated up from the ground instead of reflecting it onto the person.
source: printed key, not verified in the library; standard textbook fact (UPPSC key)

from_notes: In plants like banana, pineapple, and Chrysanthemum, lateral branches grow underground
x: Banana is propagated vegetatively by suckers, the side shoots from the underground stem. Cultivated bananas are seedless, so seeds are not an option.
source: PMF General Science Part 1 (src/science-tech/pmf-general-science-01.txt) p.99; OnlyIAS NCERT S&T Part 9 (src/science-tech/onlyias-ncert-science-tech-09.txt) p.1

x: g = GM/R², so g' = g/(0.99)² ≈ 1.02 g. The value of g rises by about 2%; it does not fall, because a smaller radius brings the surface closer to the centre.
source: derivation from g = GM/R² (NextGen Rocket Physics (src/science-tech/rocket-physics.txt))

from_notes: Nitrous oxide (N₂O) Laughing gas
x: Nitrous oxide (N2O) is laughing gas, a mild anaesthetic. Nitric oxide is NO, and the other two are higher oxides.

from_notes: Wool, being a poor conductor of heat, and having trapped air between its fibres, provides insulation.
x: Woollen clothes keep us warm mainly because air, a poor conductor, is trapped between the fibres. Books therefore key R (the protein) as false.
evidence: PMF General Science Part 7 (src/science-tech/pmf-general-science-07.txt) p.67 (wool = animal protein fibre)
dispute: Most books and keys: A true, R false (warmth comes from trapped air). Strictly: wool is a protein (keratin) fibre and itself a poor conductor (NCERT), so R is true but not the main explanation, i.e. (b).

x: Mercury has the lowest thermal conductivity here (~8 W/m·K), lower than lead (~35), zinc (~116) and copper (~400). Lead is the tempting option, but mercury is poorer still.

from_notes: carbon dioxide at night
x: At night trees cannot photosynthesise but keep respiring, so they release carbon dioxide. They do not give out carbon monoxide or sulphur dioxide.

from_notes: Solid CO₂ Dry ice
x: Dry ice is solid carbon dioxide, which sublimes without melting. It is not ice, a salt mixture or sulphur.
source: NextGen Rocket Chemistry (src/science-tech/rocket-chemistry.txt) p.2-3; PMF General Science Part 6 (src/science-tech/pmf-general-science-06.txt) p.21

from_notes: The conductivity of semiconductors increases with rise in temperature.
x: Heating frees more charge carriers, so a semiconductor's resistance decreases. A metal's resistance increases on heating.
source: PMF S&T Part 7 (src/science-tech/pmf-science-tech-07.txt) p.77; PMF General Science Part 6 (src/science-tech/pmf-general-science-06.txt) p.85

from_notes: violet light has the shortest wavelength and the highest energy
x: Violet has the shortest wavelength (~400 nm) of visible light. Blue is close but longer, and red is the longest.

from_notes: Nylon-6 Caprolactam
x: Caprolactam is the monomer from which nylon-6 is made, so it is not a polymer. Nylon, Teflon and polystyrene are polymers.

from_notes: Red light has the longest wavelength
x: Red has the longest wavelength (~700 nm) of the visible colours. Yellow, green and blue are all shorter.

from_notes: Most effective wavelength for photosynthesis Red light ~655 nm
x: Red light (~655 nm) gives the highest rate of photosynthesis. Blue is also absorbed, but green is mostly reflected.
The UPPSC key and books give red for sodium chromate (Na2CrO4). Blue, green and black are not linked to it.
evidence: local library: no entry for sodium chromate
dispute: Official key / most books: Red. Strictly: sodium chromate is a yellow solid; the orange-red salt is sodium dichromate (Wikipedia, Sigma-Aldrich).

from_notes: Copper Excellent conductivity, widely used in wires
x: Both are true: copper feels hotter because it conducts heat to the hand much faster, and copper (8.9 g/cc) is denser than glass (~2.5). Density is not the reason, so R does not explain A.

from_notes: Most effective wavelength for photosynthesis Red light ~655 nm
x: Chlorophyll absorbs mainly red and blue light and reflects green, which is why leaves look green. Options with green are therefore wrong.
UPPSC and books key both as true: without gravity there is no convection to draw in fresh air and lift the hot gases, so they say gravity is needed for a flame.
dispute: Official key / most books: both true, R explains A. Strictly: a candle does burn in microgravity with a spherical, dim blue flame (NASA); gravity only gives the flame its tear-drop shape.

from_notes: Reverberation is the persistence of sound after it has stopped. It occurs as a result of multiple re-flections
x: Reverberation comes from sound reflecting repeatedly off the walls, roof and floor, so it is felt most in large halls and churches. R explains A.
source: PMF General Science Part 6 (src/science-tech/pmf-general-science-06.txt) p.80; OnlyIAS NCERT S&T Part 6 (src/science-tech/onlyias-ncert-science-tech-06.txt) p.1

from_notes: Limestone / ... Cement, antacid
x: Limestone (~75%) is the main ingredient of cement, with clay the smaller part. Gypsum is added only to slow setting.
A goat carries its young about 150 days, less than a cow (~280), a buffalo (~310) or a camel (~390). The cow is the tempting option, but its gestation is nearly twice as long.
source: printed key, not verified in the library; standard textbook fact (ICAR animal husbandry figures)

x: The pig is a monogastric omnivore and cannot digest fibre well. Goats and cows are ruminants, and elephants are hindgut fermenters, so their gut microbes break down cellulose.
source: printed key, not verified in the library; standard textbook fact

from_notes: Rhizomes: Underground stems that produce shoots and roots (e.g., ginger, turmeric).
x: Ginger is a rhizome, an underground stem that stores food, so of these options it is a tuberous stem. It is not a root.

from_notes: Sweet potato Tuberous root
x: Sweet potato stores food in a tuberous root. Sugarcane, potato and ginger all store food in stems.
Diluting sulphuric acid and slaking quicklime with water both give out heat. Evaporation and sublimation absorb heat, so options with (i) or (iv) are wrong.
source: NCERT Class 10 Ch.1-2 (dilution of acid, CaO + H2O exothermic)

from_notes: Hydrotropism: Growth towards water.
x: Desert plants have long roots because roots grow towards water (hydrotropism), and in deserts the water lies deep. Soil heat does not cause it.

from_notes: A cell is the basic structural unit of life.
x: The cell is the basic structural and functional unit of all living things. The nucleus, DNA and chromosomes are parts inside it.
source: PMF General Science Part 1 (src/science-tech/pmf-general-science-01.txt) p.33; OnlyIAS NCERT S&T Part 8 (src/science-tech/onlyias-ncert-science-tech-08.txt) p.1

from_notes: ATP is known as the energy currency of the cell.
x: ATP is the cell's energy currency; it releases energy when it becomes ADP. ADP is the low-energy form, and RNA and DNA carry genetic information.

from_notes: Hydrometer Relative density of liquids
x: A is true because iron (sp. gr. ~7.8) is lighter than mercury (13.6) but heavier than water. R is false because iron's specific gravity is less than mercury's.
source: standard specific-gravity values; NextGen Rocket Physics (src/science-tech/rocket-physics.txt) p.35

x: Tomato belongs to Solanaceae, the same family as potato, brinjal and chilli. Gramineae is grasses, Leguminosae is pulses and Malvaceae is cotton and okra.
source: printed key, not verified in the library; standard textbook fact

x: A planimeter measures the area of a plotted map by tracing its boundary.
source: printed key, not verified in the library; standard textbook fact

x: An AB parent passes A or B and an O parent passes O, so their own children can only be A or B. The O-positive son must therefore be the adopted one.
source: Mendelian ABO inheritance (PMF General Science, genetics)

from_notes: When pH of rain water is less than 5.6, it is called acid rain
x: Distilled water left open dissolves CO2 from the air and forms carbonic acid, so its pH falls slightly below 7. It is exactly 7 only when pure and sealed.
source: OnlyIAS NCERT S&T Part 7 (src/science-tech/onlyias-ncert-science-tech-07.txt) p.1 (CO2 makes rain ~5.6)

x: Herbivores have alkaline urine (pH about 7–8) because of their plant diet. Carnivores' urine is acidic, so the lower ranges are wrong.
source: printed key, not verified in the library; standard textbook fact (veterinary physiology)

from_notes: Pyrometers: They measure high temperatures remotely by detecting infrared emissions.
x: A pyrometer measures very high temperatures (furnaces). A seismograph records earthquakes, and a xylometer measures the volume of wood.

from_notes: Fuse | Heating effect; tin-lead; in series; low melting point, high resistivity
x: Fuse wire must have a low melting point so that it melts on overcurrent. High resistivity also helps, but the low melting point is the deciding property; low resistivity and a high melting point are wrong.

from_notes: Fuse | Heating effect; tin-lead; in series; low melting point, high resistivity
x: A fuse must have a low melting point so it melts on excess current. It is connected in series, it is made of tin-lead alloy, and it cannot have a very high resistance.

from_notes: Fuse | Heating effect; tin-lead; in series; low melting point, high resistivity
x: A fuse works by the heating effect, so it must have a low melting point. It is placed in series with the circuit, not parallel, and is made of tin-lead, not silver.

from_notes: Fuse | Heating effect; tin-lead; in series; low melting point, high resistivity
x: Fuse wire has high resistance (resistivity) and a low melting point, so it heats and melts when the current is too high. A high melting point would defeat its purpose.

from_notes: Radar sensors use radio waves to detect, track, and image objects
x: Radar sends out radio waves (microwaves) and times their echoes to locate aircraft. Sound and ultrasound do not travel far in air, and light is not used.

from_notes: Ultrasonic cleaning is used to clean delicate items ... Devices emitting ultrasonic waves repel pests like rodents and insects.
x: Ultrasonic waves kill insects and bacteria, clean clothes and delicate parts, treat diseases (physiotherapy, kidney stones) and run door sensors. So all four are correct.
source: PMF General Science Part 6 (src/science-tech/pmf-general-science-06.txt) p.79; NextGen Rocket Physics (src/science-tech/rocket-physics.txt) p.78

from_notes: Synovial Fluid: Fluid present in joint cavities that lubricates and nourishes the joints.
x: Synovial fluid fills the cavities of movable joints and lubricates them. The heart has pericardial fluid; the liver and kidney have none of this kind.
source: OnlyIAS NCERT S&T Part 11 (src/science-tech/onlyias-ncert-science-tech-11.txt) p.1; PMF General Science Part 1 (src/science-tech/pmf-general-science-01.txt) p.108

from_notes: open sea using satellites and echo sounders.
x: An echo sounder (SONAR) times an ultrasound echo from the sea bed to find the depth. A decibel is a unit, and a tachometer measures rotation speed.
source: OnlyIAS NCERT S&T Part 11 (src/science-tech/onlyias-ncert-science-tech-11.txt) p.1; NextGen Rocket Physics (src/science-tech/rocket-physics.txt) p.27
